core/recipe_synth.py - turn AI-read ORDER DATA into a VERIFIED, cacheable PoRecipe.

Why this module exists
----------------------
V2.0.0 asked the LLM to *author* the ``line_pattern`` regex. Measured on one real
LPP PO, 5 independent inferences produced 4 unusable recipes (0 matched rows).
Writing a character-exact regex blind is simply not something an LLM does
reliably, and it has no way to test its own answer before replying.

So the labour is split the way V1.5 split it - and then taken one step further:

    AI    (core/ai/data_extract.py)  -> READS the PO, returns the order DATA.
    code  (this module)              -> SYNTHESIZES the extraction rule from the
                                        AI's verbatim sample rows, then REPLAYS
                                        that rule offline and hard-compares the
                                        result against the AI's data.

Only a rule that reproduces the AI's reading exactly is allowed into the
fingerprint cache. That replay gate is what makes the manual confirmation dialog
unnecessary: a broken recipe physically cannot be cached, so the next PO of the
same layout is parsed offline, zero-AI, with confidence.

Pipeline
--------
    doc_text ──► AI reads ──► ExtractedData (ground truth)
                                   │
                    locate each verbatim row back in doc_text
                                   │
              token-align the real rows: constant token -> literal,
              varying token -> named group  ⇒  line_pattern
                                   │
              same trick for the entity/PO anchor and every header field
                                   │
                        PoRecipe (candidate)
                                   │
                 replay offline: registry.parse(pages, recipe)
                                   │
        rows / total qty / per-PO qty / PO-number set must ALL match
                    ├── match    -> cache it, never call AI for this layout again
                    └── mismatch -> retry AI once with a concrete hint,
                                    then raise (never silently export bad data)

Collapse a row into (shape, runs).

    shape is e.g. ``("style", "*", "unit", "qty", "unit_price", "*")`` where
    ``*`` is a run of unclassified tokens; runs holds the tokens of each segment.

True when a run of unclassified tokens is product/colour DATA, not a
    structural label. A data word is one with an apostrophe (MEN'S / LADIES'),
    a non-ASCII token (Turkish/Cyrillic names), or a long alphabetic word
    (product nouns like TROUSERS / JACKET / BEIGE). Freezing these into a
    line_pattern literal is what makes a cached recipe die on the next PO that
    shares the layout fingerprint but carries a different product.

Pattern for a run of unclassified tokens. Returns (pattern, is_variable).

    A run is kept as a LITERAL only when it is identical on every sample row AND
    carries no digits - digits are data, and freezing data into the rule is what
    makes a cached recipe die on the next PO. Product/colour words are data too,
    so a constant run of them becomes a wildcard, not a literal. Anything else
    becomes a group.
Grow a ``line_pattern`` from the real rows. Returns (pattern, unit, used).

Escape prefix tokens, but replace data-looking ones with a wildcard.

    ``soft`` holds values that belong to OTHER extracted fields - freezing those
    into a label would make the anchor collapse the moment the next PO carries a
    different value (e.g. ``Incoterms: FOB x`` vs ``Incoterms: CIF x``).
Build (entity_anchor, po_no_anchor) from where the PO numbers actually sit.
A token that carries a VALUE rather than naming one.

The label sitting in front of a value, read right-to-left.

    Two phases, because a value is not always glued to its label:

        Supplier: 10098881 Gs Global Sourcing Co.,Ltd
        ^label^   ^phase 1^ ^value

    phase 1 swallows the data tokens wedged between the label and the value (they
    become wildcards, so a different supplier code still matches); phase 2 takes
    the label proper - its ``:`` terminator plus the words in front of it - and
    stops at the next ``:`` or the next data token, so a neighbouring field never
    leaks into the label.

Drop leading tokens that sit in front of the expected field keyword.

    ``LPP SA Supplier: 10098881`` -> ``Supplier: 10098881``: the brand tag ``LPP SA``
    is a *different* field riding the same line, so we keep only from the field
    keyword onward. Tokens are compared after stripping a trailing ``:``.

``Label: value`` -> a regex whose group(1) captures exactly ``value``.

    A value usually appears several times in a PO (multi-entity documents repeat
    the header block). We keep the LONGEST label that round-trips (most specific,
    least likely to grab the wrong field), but the *field* is chosen by the prefer
    hint: LPP prints the vendor both as ``Supplier:`` and ``Agent:`` with the same
    value - without the hint we would lock onto the shorter ``Agent:`` label and
    capture the wrong party next time. A foreign brand tag in front of the field
    keyword (``LPP SA`` before ``Supplier:``) is trimmed away.

Map ``{printed quantity -> printed amount}`` for two-number total rows.

    An LPP block total prints as a bare, UNLABELLED two-number row::

        8000 81,600.00        <- Quantity | Total Amount

    Nothing on that row names its columns, so a model asked for the block total
    sometimes copies the AMOUNT instead of the QUANTITY. Collect every row of
    that exact shape, so :func:`verify_recipe` can recognise the misread rather
    than blame the parser - whose figure is the sum of the printed detail rows
    and is the correct one.

    The shape is deliberately narrow (an optional TOTAL-ish word, then exactly
    one bare integer and one 2-decimal money token) so genuine detail rows,
    which always carry a style code, a colour and a unit, can never match.

True when ``expected`` is the AMOUNT printed beside quantity ``parsed``.

    That combination means the document itself corroborates the parser: the row
    it summed to ``parsed`` is printed verbatim, and the model's disagreeing
    figure is simply the neighbouring money column.

Return the layout_type the current structural detectors would choose.

    This is a cheap, parser-free mirror of the structural branch in
    ``acquire_recipe``. It lets the UI invalidate a cached recipe when the
    app's detector set has changed (e.g. a new layout is added or an old one
    is split), so a stale ``matrix_percarton`` cache can never block the new
    ``frankie_ecom`` detector.

    layout is parsed offline with zero AI calls. On failure this raises rather
    than exporting numbers nobody has checked.
